sections.h2: Selling a Del Rio house without a long wait
sections.html:
A broker's listing, a sale you manage yourself and a quick deal with a cash purchaser are the three choices. Listings take longer to turn up a buyer, whereas cash gives you the say over when you close.

Start by pulling together the deed, your lender's payoff letter, the latest tax bill and old permit records. Every written offer needs to name the price and closing date, say who covers title and recording costs, and describe the condition the buyer wants at handover.

  • Check if the buyer plans an inspection before the offer becomes firm.
  • Decide whether furniture and appliances stay or go.
  • Have the closing date written down.

sections.h2: What buyers see in Del Rio housing
sections.html: Del Rio lies on U.S. Highway 90 at the spot where the Rio Grande and San Felipe Creek meet, 154 miles west of San Antonio. It incorporated on November 15, 1911, and counted 33,867 people in 2000. The oldest homes sit near the creek. Housing later shifted north of the rail line, and the retail strip along Highway 90 and the reservoir built in the 1960s tugged growth north once more. Describe your block with that pattern in mind, and refer school zoning questions to the school district.

sections.h2: Permit steps for a home project
sections.html:
The Development Services Department reviews plans and issues building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, sign and garage sale permits. Its inspectors also look at substandard buildings, and it grants certificates of occupancy.

Codes in force include the 2024 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Plumbing, Fire, Energy Conservation and Fuel and Gas codes, the 2024 Property Maintenance Code and the 2020 National Electrical Code. A garage conversion or addition built with no permit should be disclosed to the buyer, and the city can explain how to close that file.

sections.h2: Val Verde County tax bills at closing
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1, and the lien for the year attaches the same day. Bills go in the mail around October 1. Owners may split payment, with half due by November 30 and half by June 30, although most bills must be paid by January 31.

Property records sit with the Val Verde County appraisal district and tax office, and the city home page links to its tax department. A seller who never claimed a homestead exemption leaves that option open to a buyer closing later in the year. Ask the title company to show how the year's bill is split between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: Selling a rental that has a tenant
sections.html:
Texas lays out a clear sequence when a tenant will not leave. The landlord delivers written notice to vacate, usually three days unless the lease sets another period, and then files in justice court. The tenant must be served at least four days before trial, and the hearing lands 10 to 21 days after filing.

Either side may appeal to county court within five days of the judgment. Six days after final judgment a writ of possession can issue, an officer serves it within five days, and the tenant gets 24 hours of notice before removal. People who buy occupied houses will want the lease, deposit records and rent history. Some owners sell with the lease still running, and a landlord going that way should talk with the tenant early about showings.

Heirs can open probate on a will within four years of a death, rely on a muniment of title when no administration is required, or sign a small estate affidavit when there is no will, the assets are $75,000 or less and every heir agrees. A transfer on death deed signed and filed while the owner lived avoids probate entirely.

On a loan in default, lenders typically hold off until the loan is more than 120 days late. You then have 20 days to bring it current, and the lender must post the sale notice three weeks or more before the first-Tuesday auction. Any surplus is paid to junior liens first and then to the owner. Request an exact payoff from the servicer before anything else.

sections.h2: City permits and licenses that can touch a sale
sections.html:
Development Services also hands out garage sale and sign permits, so an estate sale or moving sale may require one. The city has a business license service as well, and its business pages carry a hotel occupancy tax application for lodging operators. If guests ever stayed in the house by the night, ask whether those pages apply to you before closing.

Utilities run through the city, which handles billing and residential waste collection. Get a final bill and a stop-service date so the buyer begins with a clean account.

sections.h2: Filing the deed and closing day
sections.html: The Val Verde County Clerk records the deed after a notary has acknowledged it. Most title companies file it for you and pay the recording charge from the settlement funds. At the table you will sign the deed and the settlement statement, hand over the keys and openers, and receive your proceeds once any payoff and tax settlement are taken out.

faqs.q: Does Del Rio require a permit for home repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, when the work falls under the adopted codes: building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and sign work. Development Services reviews plans, issues permits, inspects and signs off with a certificate of occupancy.

faqs.q: Who buys houses in Del Rio?
faqs.a: Local families, military households, landlords and cash purchasers all shop here. Offers from a financed buyer, an agent's advice and a cash quote will show you who is active at your price.

faqs.q: Which office files a Del Rio deed?
faqs.a: The Val Verde County Clerk, once the signature has been properly acknowledged. Your title company typically files it and pays the fee from closing funds.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Del Rio eviction finish?
faqs.a: A justice court hearing falls 10 to 21 days after filing, and an officer cannot remove anyone until at least six days after judgment. Notice, service and appeals add time, so plan on several weeks.

faqs.q: Can Del Rio heirs sell without full probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A small estate affidavit, a muniment of title or a transfer on death deed filed before the owner died can each work. Ask the county clerk and a title company which one a buyer will accept.
